title: Unify provisioning error model and compact reconciler shape for GPU autoscaler
creator: Priya Ramachandran
description: Background: Over the last 18 months the autoscaler and capacity planner codepaths have accreted multiple provisioning adapters, ad-hoc error types, and two concurrent reconcilers (lease-based and snapshot-merge). This has increased latency spikes during scale-up, caused duplicated provisioning attempts, and made reasoning about node lifecycle transitions difficult. Goal: consolidate the provisioning error model into a single canonical set of error classes, and replace the dual-reconciler surface with a compact event-driven reconciler shape that reduces goroutine churn and centralizes retry/fallback logic. Expected outcomes: fewer duplicate provisioning requests, lower reconciliation latency p50/p95, easier debugging (single error taxonomy in logs), and a smaller migration surface for Dedicated/Private deployments.
steps: Design: finalize canonical error taxonomy and mapping from legacy adaptors
Implementation: extract error adapter layer and introduce errors.ProvisionReason enum
Reconciler: implement compact event-driven reconciler with single reconciliation loop per node group
Migration shim: compatibility layer to accept legacy leasepool API for 8 weeks
Testing: unit tests for error mappings, integration tests against capacity-planner simulator
Benchmarking: synthetic scale tests (1k/5k/10k nodes) to measure reconc latency and duplicate-provision rate
Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 10% prod -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on regression
